summary: Bethesda's open-world fantasy RPG series, including mainline games, Travels mobile entries, online/card/mobile spin-offs, and current remasters.

primary.why: Arena shipped for MS-DOS only; DOSBox is the practical preservation route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the DOS release through DOSBox using a legally preserved copy or Bethesda's free legacy release where available.

entries.title: The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall

emulation.notes: Use DOSBox only for original-release study.

primary.why: The original release is MS-DOS, but Daggerfall Unity/GOG Cut is the best modern archive route with higher-fidelity rendering and extensive fixes.
primary.how_to_play: Use Daggerfall Unity or the GOG Cut with the original game data; document mods if using the GOG package.

entries.remaster_caveats: Community recreation/package; preserve original data and mod list.

entries.title: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind
entries.definitive_edition: Morrowind Game of the Year Edition on Windows/OpenMW

primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows GOTY edition through Steam/GOG or OpenMW with original data; document any mods.

entries.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
entries.definitive_edition: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered

primary.why: Oblivion Remastered includes the original DLC, Knights of the Nine, and Shivering Isles with a modern visual overhaul; Windows is the most flexible high-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Oblivion Remastered on Windows with the current patch and Deluxe/standard content noted; use original GOTY only for mod/tool compatibility study.

entries.remaster_caveats: Remastered does not officially support modding; preserve original GOTY for legacy modded play.

entries.title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

primary.why: Windows Anniversary Edition includes Special Edition, the three expansions, and Creation Club/Anniversary content while preserving the broadest mod/fix route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Skyrim Anniversary Edition on Windows; document patch, Creation Club content, and mod list if used.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document mods and Creation Club/Anniversary content; VR is a side route, not the main complete playthrough.

entries.title: The Elder Scrolls Online

primary.why: ESO is a live MMO across PC/Mac and consoles; Windows is the best archive/capture route with the current chapter/update state.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows client; document server, chapter ownership, subscription state, and patch.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document server, chapter ownership, subscription state, and patch.

entries.title: The Elder Scrolls: Legends

primary.why: Legends launched on Windows before mobile/Mac and shut down on January 30, 2025, so Windows is only a historical preservation target.
primary.how_to_play: No current normal play route after shutdown; preserve client/media for documentation only.

entries.remaster_caveats: Delisted/shut down; not a current play recommendation.

entries.title: The Elder Scrolls: Blades

primary.why: Blades launched on Android/iOS and later Switch; it is scheduled to shut down June 30, 2026, so Android is only a short-term/mobile preservation target.
primary.how_to_play: Play before the June 30, 2026 shutdown if still accessible; document account/build state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Shutdown scheduled; no durable current route after service closure.

entries.title: The Elder Scrolls: Castles

primary.why: Castles is a mobile management spin-off on Android and iOS; Android is selected as the practical archive/mobile route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Android release and document build/account state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Free-to-play mobile title; preserve build/account state.

primary.why: The Elder Scrolls VI is announced and in development, but it has no release date or final platform/version behavior as of 2026-06-15.
primary.how_to_play: Do not choose a definitive play route until the game ships and final editions/platforms are verified.
